There's an existing functionality for 1 angular limit. 

I have a second pr for multiple angular limits

From a cursory look at the code, the design looks good overall. I'd be in favor of merging for 4.7

I need to test and review the math and we can discuss this at the meeting this coming weekend.

Code has some unused code and comments, and failing static checks, so when you get a chance, would help to get the code ready for review

> There is no setting to disable this feature.

I don't know of many users of spring bones yet: it is relatively new. Still, in case a user reports fredback that this breaks their project or we need to offer the option for some reason, I would be curious if it would be possible to disable the feature by passing the same coordinate twice for the two ends of the capsule (making it a sphere). i think we shouldn't add a disable unless someone gives feedback requesting it.

> capsule...

I would appreciate if you are able to prototype what this implementation would look like (find the closest sphere) But I personally do not think we need to block on this. Open to other opinions.

> plane...

Probably not an issue because I don't think we handle the case where the plane is in between two joints in a spring bones chain. And the common case is all joints are on one side of a plane in which case there is no difference between sphere and capsule collision.

> inside...

Same reasoning as plane: the whole chain should be on one side of the collider so there is no difference between sphere and capsule collision

> There is no setting to disable this feature. As I mentioned in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/14581#issuecomment-4184947668, this PR with current state can **NEVER be merged** as is. This is because it would break compatibility with past projects and VRM. Furthermore, it seems like this PR does not currently support capsule collisions, allowing such a breaking change here would lead to even greater compatibility issues in the future if capsule collisions are updated to handle this behavior. Judging from the reactions on social media, I believe SpringBone is already being used to some extent. Also, in VRM, I often see settings that make heavy use of inside colliders, based on the premise that there is no collision between joint spheres. For example https://yananann-hatenadiary-jp.translate.goog/entry/2018/11/17/195631?_x_tr_sl=ja&_x_tr_tl=en&_x_tr_hl=en&_x_tr_pto=wapp (although it is DynamicBone not SpringBone) In short, inside collider is often used as an external angle limiter or applied to accessories for enclosing objects inside bottles. > capsule... plane... inside... Considering that support for most of the collision shapes are not supported with this option, I think making this an enum option for sphere collision is the best way to prevent confusion. How about calling it chain mode? ```cpp enum CollideMode { COLLIDE_MODE_NORMAL, // DEFAULT, JOINT or any other name... COLLIDE_MODE_INSIDE, COLLIDE_MODE_CHAIN, // CONNECTED, TAPERED or any other name... } ``` So, the option should be placed on the SpringBoneCollision (only SpringBoneCollisionSphere) side rather than the SpringBoneSimulator side. With this method, it is clear that it can only be used with SpringBoneCollisionSphere. With this method, it is safely possible to step by step add chain collision support to other collision shapes (such as SpringBoneCollisionCapsule) without breaking compatibility in the future. We need to think a little about how to represent it visually with a Gizmo, but one idea would be to draw a capsule that connects between joints in a color different from the joints sphere, and make the chain mode collision a color in a similar to that, like: Currently, the inside mode collision is purple, so for example, it is okay to change that inside collision to dark blue and set the chain mode to purple.

It is likely a value unrelated to the Verlet integration formula, so it might be better to manage it separately from VerletInfo.
For example, you could create something like ConnectionInfo and define the default as `ConnectionInfo *connection = nullptr;`. Then, you can save memory by only performing memnew and drawing the Gizmo for the connection if the child CollisionShape includes a ChainMode. Although it's just three floats, it's a minor matter, so if it's not always necessary, calculating it on the fly when need to update gizmo might be sufficient.

Also, note that for performance reasons, the Gizmo calculation should not be performed every frame; it needs to be implemented such that it is calculated only once and then bound to the skin. Also if that information is not needed at runtime, you can use `#ifndef TOOLS_ENABLED`.

@goatchurchprime As I mentioned above, please proceed with the work on the assumption that CollideMode must be implemented in SpringBoneCollision, not SpringBoneSimulator. This has already been discussed and agreed upon within the animation team, including myself and @lyuma.
